title: The publisher who bought a whole show to get one tune
summary: Fats told him how Robbins bought a Broadway show that had gone to Paris just to obtain one tune and still made a quarter million.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Do you know if any of this man's tunes every became hits because Fats played them?

Yes. Yes, because -- I'm trying to think of the publisher, because he was a little publisher himself, but the big guys had snowed him under, you know. He would say -- get to where he couldn't move. He couldn't -- you know. Because Fats told me the story about some man had a tune, and sold it to a show, Broadway show, and somebody in Robbins, Robbins himself, wanted the doggone tune, and he couldn't get it.
So the show went to Paris, went to Europe, and it was doing fine, so Robbins went over there and bought the whole doggone show to get this tune, and he still made a quarter of a million.
You know what the tune was?
Hmm, Fats told me, because he was telling us in the club. And by golly, I forgot what the hell was that. he bought the show to get this tune, and still made a quarter of a million dollars. (Laughs.)
Well it must have been some tune!
Yeah. See, so I mean those -- I said boy, this is really something. And --
